title: Find the third angle with a parallel line
description: A line is drawn through the top corner parallel to the base, and the alternate angles give two of the three angles on a straight line. The third angle is what remains of one hundred and eighty degrees. Keeko's doubt is that both alternate angles are fifty degrees.
teaching_notes: One idea: a line through the top corner parallel to the base turns the two base angles into alternate angles, and the three angles on that line make a straight angle. Watch for students who give both alternate angles the same value.

source: Consider a triangle ABC with ∠B = 50° and ∠C = 70°. Let us see how we can find ∠A without construction. Let us suppose we construct a line XY parallel to BC through vertex A. ∠XAB = ∠B and ∠YAC = ∠C, because they are alternate angles of the transversals AB and AC. We know that ∠XAB, ∠YAC and ∠BAC together form 180°. So ∠XAB + ∠YAC + ∠BAC = 180°, 50° + ∠BAC + 70° = 180°, 120° + ∠BAC = 180°. Thus, ∠BAC = 60°.
video_script.why: The child has seen that the third angle does not depend on the length of the side and now finds it without any drawing.
video_script.substitution: The book's own triangle with fifty degrees at bee and seventy degrees at cee.
video_script.anchor: triangle ABC with fifty degrees at B and seventy degrees at C, and a line XY through A parallel to BC
video_script.wrong_answer: both alternate angles are fifty degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees both alternate angles sit on the same line and gives them the same value, but each one matches the base angle on its own side.
video_script.payoff_line: The angle at eigh is sixty degrees

final_answer.spoken: the angle at eigh is sixty degrees

maths_rules: XY is parallel to BC, so ∠XAB = ∠B = 50° and ∠YAC = ∠C = 70° (alternate angles)
∠XAB, ∠BAC and ∠YAC together make the straight angle XAY: 50° + ∠BAC + 70° = 180°
check: a construction with 50° at B and 70° at C gives 60° at A
